headline: High: Cline’s default workspace write/network/MCP powers can conflict with Pathway’s read-only, no-network profile, while shared filesystem coupling creates prompt-injection and cascading-error risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline can read/write workspace files and use MCP, so it may ingest attacker-controlled content from shared files or tool outputs. Pathway has no file or network I/O, so it is not itself an injection source, but it can still be a downstream consumer if wired into the same workspace. The shared-filesystem bridge makes the pathway plausible in default coding setups.
conditions: IF both agents share the same workspace directory, THEN file content from one can influence the other.
IF Cline parses workspace files or MCP payloads as instructions, THEN prompt injection is possible.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Disable MCP servers that ingest untrusted content.
Add provenance tags to files before Cline reads them.
Require manual review of any file-based instructions.
Use read-only mounts for Pathway inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline touches source code and browser screenshots and has broad network egress, so sensitive workspace data could leave the machine if it is pointed at confidential files. Pathway has no filesystem read or network egress, so it does not add a second leakage path. The pair only becomes risky when the shared workspace contains sensitive data, making the blast radius limited but real.
conditions: IF the shared workspace contains secrets or regulated data, THEN Cline can transmit them over network egress.
IF Pathway is given sensitive inputs through an external pipeline, THEN its outputs may reflect that data even though it cannot exfiltrate directly.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace.
Restrict Cline to a scrubbed repo clone.
Block outbound network except approved model endpoints.
Mount Pathway inputs read-only.
Scan files for secrets before Cline opens them.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cline can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; Pathway cannot write or modify anything. That asymmetry reduces direct contention, but Cline’s workspace-scoped shared state via filesystem means concurrent edits can still collide if Pathway or its pipeline writes into the same tree through external orchestration. Uncertainty remains because Pathway’s runtime write surfaces are undocumented.
conditions: IF Pathway is wrapped by an external job that writes into Cline’s workspace, THEN file collisions can occur.
IF both agents target the same git checkout, THEN Cline can race with external writes.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Serialize git writes with a lock file.
Make Pathway outputs append-only.
Run Cline on a branch per task.
Use a coordinator to arbitrate shared paths.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can generate code or file edits that Pathway may later consume if the operator wires them together, and Pathway’s document-processing role suggests it may treat upstream artifacts as authoritative inputs. Because Pathway’s verification behavior is undocumented, the safer choice is medium rather than low. The pair can propagate a bad artifact across stages even without direct action authority.
conditions: IF Cline writes an incorrect artifact into a shared handoff file, THEN Pathway can process the error downstream.
IF Pathway is configured to trust upstream files without validation, THEN cascading error occurs.
mitigations: Add schema validation between stages.
Require checksum or signature checks on handoff files.
Insert a human review step before Pathway ingestion.
Log and diff Cline outputs before reuse.
Reject files that fail basic sanity checks.

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent, so only a limited compliance concern is visible. Cline handles model-provider API keys and browser screenshots, while Pathway’s profile lists no data classes or controls; that asymmetry suggests possible policy mismatch if regulated data is introduced, but the evidence is too thin for medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in Cline’s workspace, THEN its browser screenshots or model calls may create policy obligations.
IF Pathway is used on the same regulated dataset without documented retention controls, THEN compliance gaps may appear.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Cline sessions.
Document retention for both tools.
Use separate datasets for regulated workflows.
Review vendor DPAs before deployment.
Mask screenshots before storage.
